- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤ 0.33), model tends to underestimate; increase forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model often overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction: reduce forecast by 2–5% in the following 2–3 periods.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, consider mean reversion bias; adjust downward by 1–2% per period until convergence.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; apply a “sentiment pivot” rule: reduce forecast by 2–4% in the next 3 periods if sentiment drops below 0.33.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment; apply a “lagged sentiment” filter: weight recent sentiment (last 3–5 days) more heavily than distant sentiment for correction.
